Example demonstrating how Opacus v1.0 API can be used with PyTorch Lightning. This is a follow-up for #244. 

## Changes

Added `mnist_lightning.py` with the classifier allowing training with DP. 

TODO:
- [x] Fix the problem with `forbid_accumulation_hook`
- [ ] Fix attaching GradSampleModule twice when using LightningCLI
- [ ] Poisson sampling: check the data loader is consistend with the optimizer
- [ ] Correctly handle DDP (raise NotImplementedError, for example)
- [ ] Add a guide on adding DP to Lightning code in the docstring

## What about Full Integration with Lightning?

There are two levels of integration:
1. Provide PL users with a straightforward and clean way to add DP training by **modifying** their `LightningModule`.
2. Provide PL users with a **seamless** solution "turn on privacy" working on the Trainer level and requiring no changes inside `LightningModule`. 

Having a **seamless** integration is desirable as this 1) lowers the entry threshold to a minimum (thus making privacy-in-ML a commodity not magic); 2) preserves the separation of logical parts promoted by PL.

Having a **modify-module** integration is a MUST. The lack of it will force PL users to rewrite their code to pure torch, thus discouraging usage of privacy-preserving training.

## How do we build a Full Integration?

Below are my thoughts after exploring ways of implementing integration with PL. This doesn't pretend to be a detailed analysis, just thoughts. 

Prototypes for the old API:

1. Modify-module #244
    - ✅ Clean & straightforward
    - Main methods of LitghtningModule remains unchanged (forward, configure_optimizers, training/test_step)
    - DP is enabled by attaching PrivacyEngine to the optimizer in `on_train_start` method
2. Seamless [romovpa/#5](https://github.com/romovpa/opacus/pull/5)
    - ✅ Clean and straightforward
    - No changes in LightningModule is required
    - DP is enabled by adding a special callback to the `pl.Trainer`
    - If LightningDataModule is used, we enable poisson sampling by wrapping the data module.

The anticipated v1.0 API moves from attach/inject architecture to wrap/extend. At least on first approach, this creates an obstacle for integrating with PL:

1. Modify-module #250 (this PR)
     - ✅ Straightforward & clean enough.
     - DP is enabled by calling `make_private()` in `configure_optimizers()` to convert the optimizer to DP version
     - 👌 No direct way to access training data in LightningModule, have to use private fields (not good). Solving [this issue](https://github.com/PyTorchLightning/pytorch-lightning/issues/10430) will help. Folks from the Lightning team assured me that the dataloader will be officially available in `trainer` eventually. In this case it is safe to proceed with the hack.
2. Subclass-module (next PR)
    - ✅ Straightforward & clean
    - DP is enabled via inheriting from `DPLightningModule` which hides pre-defined parameters and necessary wrappings from the users.
3. Seamless (future)
    - 🤔  Requires integrating **INTO** Lightning
        - DP will be enabled via Trainer settings and implemented directly in `trainer.fit(model, data)`.
        - 💪 Opacus must be a dependency of Lightning which is a big step. We need to get community support. We must ensure stability of the main branch.
        - Can we use standard extension mechanisms? No.
            - [Callback](https://pytorch-lightning.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extensions/callbacks.html): we cannot wrap model/optimizer. Although we can use callback to attach/add hooks (see [this](https://github.com/romovpa/opacus/pull/5)).
            - [TrainingTypePlugin](https://pytorch-lightning.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extensions/plugins.html#training-type-plugins): intended to customize training running in parallel on many machines.


## Other questions 

- ‼️ Not clear how to combine Opacus' distributed modules and PL's. PL is designed to separate the model from the training implementation, so DDP is deeply under the hood.


## Related

- Forum discussion: [PyTorch Lightning Support](https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/pytorch-lightning-support/113507/5)
- Lightning issue: [Add a callback to support ocapus](https://github.com/PyTorchLightning/pytorch-lightning/issues/3305)
- Lightning issue: [Unable to access datalaoders within configure_optimizers](https://github.com/PyTorchLightning/pytorch-lightning/issues/10430)

proposed solution: allow specifying custom media type in generated spec
on both controller level by:
  - using new `@Produces` decorator

and on method level by:
  - using new `@Produces` decorator

author: adamvictorclever
body:
Very minor, but I noticed that the `close` method on the js client is currently typed as `close()` in the TypeScript types. While the intent was that it should have no return value, what this actually means is that the return value is unspecified. In general, it defaults to `any` and will cause a `noImplicitAny` violation, although the violation is largely a non-issue since we usually run the TS compiler with `skipLibCheck`.

This fixes the type to indicate that it returns nothing. It's a minor fix, but I figured I'd make it while I noticed.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution to Grapl! Please take some time

### Which issue does this PR correspond to?
https://github.com/grapl-security/issue-tracker/issues/774

<!-- Please provide a link to the GitHub Issue this pull request is
meant to address. -->

### What changes does this PR make to Grapl? Why?
This adds basic consul intentions and the ability to deploy these intentions in a managed manner.

Consul Intentions should be thought of as a service to service firewall. It supports L4 rules (allow or deny traffic from one service to another) and  L7 rules (Allow or deny traffic based on any combination of path, header or method). This will likely become more important as we implement plugins or expand the number of services supported.

Design:
Intentions are currently manually created within the nomad/intentions folder as json files.
Pulumi then takes the directory of these config files reads them in one by one and creates corresponding Consul Intentions dynamically.

Potential future work: Autogenerating stubbed files based on Nomad definitions

rationale behind them. This will help us understand your approach to
solving the problem. -->

Deployed these changes to AWS sandbox and checked that intentions were created in consul

author: alisinabh
body:
Hello everyone,

I've had an idea and I wanted to share it with you before working more on that to see if you like it or not.

Basically this module can generate Elixir modules from ABI specs. So you can use them closer to how you use them with web3.js

### Example

```elixir
iex> ExW3.DynamoContract.generate_module(ERC20, "priv/erc20.abi.json")
iex> ERC20.symbol |> ERC20.call(to: "0x6b1...71d0f")
{:ok, ["DAI"]}
```

The other benefit from this approach is it can also be done at compile time and have no runtime penalty.

Please let me know if you think this is a good approach so I can continue working on it.

Have a good one.

author: naros
body:
https://issues.redhat.com/browse/DBZ-4169

This PR introduces support for customized cache configurations with Infinispan.  This PR specifically removes the config option `log.mining.buffer.type.location` in favor of user-supplied XML configurations for each cache:

New configuration properties include
- `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.cache.transactions`
- `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.cache.commited_transactions`
- `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.cache.rollback_transactions`
- `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.cache.schema_changes`
- `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.cache.events`

Furthermore with the introduction of remote cache support, the `log.mining.buffer.type` value-set has been adjusted so that the `infinispan` option has been deprecated and is synonymous with the new `infinispan_embedded` value.   A new value of  `infinispan_remote` has been included to dictate using a remote configuration.

The remote implementation relies on the Hotrod client and this client must be configured with the server endpoint and with any necessary authentication.  To allow this configuration to be supplied in a flexible way, the connector will take all settings that are part of the `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.client` namespace and pass them to the Hotrod client removing the special prefix of `log.mining.buffer.`.  

I thought about using the existence of `log.mining.buffer.infinispan.client.*` settings to derive whether the Infinspan impl is to use embedded or the Hotrod client mode; but for now left it as discussed above.  If you guys think its fine to use the existence of the properties to resolve whether to use embedded or remote caches, that's a relatively simple change to make.

Lastly, the following are still outstanding tasks:
- [x] Update documentation; including example configurations for both embedded and remote cache modes
- [x] Use configurable options for Infinispan server docker image
- [x] Flush out `Field` definitions for cache configurations
- [x] Fix `OracleConnectorConfigDefTest` errors due to configuration validations
- [x] Consolidate `CacheProvider` into the processor implementations?
- [x] Extract default Hotrod settings as static values in `TestHelper`?

Since we may want to get this into Alpha2 this week, I wanted to get the ball going on the review/input asap.

### Update [docutils](https://pypi.org/project/docutils) from **0.17.1** to **0.18**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 0.18b1
   ```
   ===========================

.. Note::

   Docutils 0.18.x is the last version supporting Python 2.7 and 3.5.


* Output changes:

  Identifiers:
    During `identifier normalization`_, leading number and hyphen
    characters are no longer stripped from a `reference name`_, if the
    id_prefix_ setting is non-empty.

    Example:
      with ``--id-prefix="DU-"``, a section with title "34. May"
      currently gets the identifier key ``DU-may`` and after the
      change the identifier key ``DU-34-may``.

    The default value for the auto_id_prefix_ setting changed to ``%``:
    "use the tag name as prefix for auto-generated IDs".
    Set auto_id_prefix_ to ``id`` for unchanged auto-IDs.

  HTML5:
    Use the semantic tag <aside> for footnote text and citations, topics
    (except abstract and toc), admonitions, and system messages.
    Use <nav> for the Table of Contents.

    Make "auto" table column widths the default: Only specify column
    widths, if the `"widths" option`_ is set and not "auto".
    The table-style__ setting "colwidths-grid" restores the current default.

    .. _"widths" option: __ docs/ref/rst/directives.htmltable
    __ docs/user/config.htmltable-style

    Items of a definition list with class argument "details" are
    converted to `details disclosure elements`_. Example::

      ..class:: details

      Summary
        This additional information should be hidden.

    Do not add "compound-first", "compound-middle", or "compound-last" to
    elements nested in a compound. Use child selector and ":first-child",
    ":last-child" pseudo classes instead.
    Use class value "backrefs" instead of "fn-backref" for a span of
    back-references.

    Write footnote brackets and field term colons to HTML, so that they
    are present also without CSS and when copying text.

    Move space character between section number and heading into
    "sectnum" span.

  math-output: html
    Support more commands, fix mapping of commands to Unicode characters.
    Scale variable sized operators and big delimiters with CSS.
    Don't use <tt> element (deprecated in HTML5).
    Use STIX fonts if available.

  LaTeX:
     `legacy_class_functions`_ setting default changed to "False":
     admonitions are now environments.

* New standard Docutils doctree node "meta__".

* New configuration setting: [latex writers] legacy_column_widths_.

* Removed files:

  - ``iepngfix.htc`` and ``blank.gif`` (IEÂ 6 workaround for `s5_html`).

* Removed function: ``utils.unique_combinations``
  (obsoleted by ``itertools.combinations``).

* Removed attribute: ``HTMLTranslator.topic_classes``
  (check node.parent.classes instead).

* Major refactoring and fixes/additions in
  ``docutils/utils/math/math2html.py`` and
  ``docutils/utils/math/latex2mathml.py``
  (mathematical notation in HTML, cf. `LaTeX syntax for mathematics`_).

* ``nodes.Node.traverse()`` returns an iterator instead of a list.

* Various bugfixes and improvements (see HISTORY_).

__ docs/ref/doctree.htmlmeta
.. _identifier normalization:

.. _id_prefix: docs/user/config.htmlid-prefix
.. _auto_id_prefix: docs/user/config.htmlauto-id-prefix
.. _details disclosure elements:

.. _LaTeX syntax for mathematics: docs/ref/rst/mathematics.html
.. _legacy_column_widths: docs/user/config.htmllegacy-column-widths

We'll know if this works based on whether or not the AppVeyor build
works.

body: There are a lot of different rules that are defined within `Magento2/Sniffs/Annotation/MethodArgumentsSniff.php`. These all were reported as the same generic `Magento2.Annotation.MethodArguments.MethodArguments`; now these have a descriptive rule name, such as `Magento2.Annotation.MethodArguments.ParamOrder` or `Magento2.Annotation.MethodArguments.ExtraParam`.
